tasks.title: Add rate limiting and input sanitization to API endpoints
tasks.description: Implement a request‑rate‑limiting middleware (e.g., express‑rate‑limit) in server.js to protect public endpoints from brute‑force and DoS attacks. Add a validation layer using a schema library (e.g., Joi) in src/lib/db.js and route handlers to sanitize and validate all incoming parameters (search queries, booking dates, user IDs). This prevents injection attacks and ensures only well‑formed data reaches the database.
acceptance: Requests exceeding 100 per minute from the same IP receive HTTP 429 responses.
All API payloads are validated against defined Joi schemas; malformed requests return HTTP 400 with a clear error message.
No SQL injection or XSS payload can be persisted in the database (verified with automated security tests).

tasks.title: Introduce DB connection pooling and in‑memory caching for listings
tasks.description: Refactor src/lib/db.js to use a connection pool (e.g., pg‑pool for PostgreSQL) instead of creating a new client per request, reducing latency and resource usage. Add a simple LRU cache (e.g., node‑cache) for the most‑requested listings (GET /listings) and search results, with a TTL of 5 minutes. Update server.js to serve cached data when available and fall back to the DB otherwise.
acceptance: Database connections are reused; the number of active connections never exceeds the pool size (e.g., 20).
Cache hit rate for listings is at least 60% in load tests.
Response time for GET /listings drops by ≥30% compared to baseline (measured with a simple load test).

tasks.title: iCal Calendar Sync for Listings
tasks.description: Add iCal integration so hosts can export their listing availability as an .ics feed and import external calendar events. Extend the users table with an `externalCalendarUrl` column. Implement a new module `src/lib/calendarSync.js` that (a) generates an iCal feed from current bookings (GET /api/listings/:id/ical), (b) receives webhook POSTs with iCal data (POST /api/calendar-sync/webhook) and parses events, (c) creates or updates bookings while respecting existing reservations and invoking `validateBookingConflict` from `bookingEngine`. Schedule a periodic job (using `node-cron` or similar) to fetch external iCal URLs and reconcile conflicts. Update `server.js` to register the new routes and middleware, and expose a simple UI button in the host dashboard (`src/components/HostDashboard.jsx`) to copy the iCal URL and toggle sync.
acceptance: GET /api/listings/:id/ical returns a valid .ics file containing all confirmed bookings for that listing.
POST /api/calendar-sync/webhook with a valid iCal payload creates new bookings or updates existing ones without causing overlapping reservations.
The `users` table now has an `externalCalendarUrl` TEXT column and the DB schema migration runs without errors.
Host dashboard displays a 'Sync Calendar' button that copies the iCal URL to clipboard and shows a toggle indicating sync status.

tasks.title: Push Notification Engine for Real‑time Guest & Host Alerts
tasks.description: Create a unified push‑notification subsystem. Add a `notifications` table in SQLite (id, userId, type, title, body, isRead, createdAt). Implement `src/lib/notificationEngine.js` with functions `createNotification`, `getUserNotifications`, `markNotificationRead`. Extend `server.js` to expose a GraphQL mutation `sendNotification` and a subscription (via the existing WebSocket chat server) that pushes new notifications to connected clients. In the React side, add `src/components/NotificationToast.jsx` that renders toast messages and a notification bell UI. Update `src/App.jsx` to initialize a WebSocket listener on mount, dispatch incoming notifications to a global state, and show the toast component. Ensure that when a booking status changes to "confirmed" or "canceled", the backend calls `createNotification` for the relevant host and guest, and the frontend displays the toast within 2 seconds. Persist notifications so they appear in the existing `InboxModal` when opened.
acceptance: Creating a booking with status 'confirmed' triggers a toast notification for both host and guest within 2 seconds of the mutation response.
Notifications are stored in the SQLite `notifications` table and are listed correctly when the user opens the InboxModal.
